title: Synchronization of log tower centers on surjective etale covers
statement:
Let $u:(U,N)\to(X,M)$ be a surjective strict etale morphism of locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup, def-weil-etale-morphism]. For a finite saturated log blowup tower $B_\bullet$ over $X$ with ordered nonempty coherent centers $I_i\subset M_i$, form its recursive uncontracted pullback $A_\bullet$ over $U$ [def-trf-strict-etale-log-blowup-procedure]. At every level $A_i\to B_i$ is the scheme-theoretic base change of $u$, hence surjective strict etale. The pulled-back center is the whole source log monoid sheaf if and only if $I_i=M_i$. Thus a contracted tower, meaning one with no whole-monoid center, retains every stage under a surjective strict etale pullback. A whole-monoid center has an identity log blowup and remains whole after every fs log pullback. A proper principal center is retained, even when its blowup is an isomorphism.

Let $\mathcal T$ be a strict etale log blowup procedure on charted admissible inputs [def-trf-strict-etale-log-blowup-procedure]. Every assigned tower is contracted, and its tower on the empty input has length zero. Suppose $X$ is an admissible input and $u:U\to X$ is a surjective strict etale cover such that $U$, $R=U\times_XU$ and $P=U\times_XU\times_XU$ are charted admissible inputs. Put $S=\mathcal T(U)$, of length $n$. Both full pullbacks $p_1^*S,p_2^*S$ to $R$ have length $n$ and the prescribed comparisons identify them with $\mathcal T(R)$. Their induced ordered isomorphism $\theta:p_1^*S\simeq p_2^*S$ preserves the actual ideal centers as subideals of the identified log structures, restricts to the identity along the diagonal, and satisfies $\theta_{23}\theta_{12}=\theta_{13}$ on $P$. In particular it gives an uncontracted descent datum with the common stage index set $0,\ldots,n-1$, including the centers.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.11, p.108 and proof of 3.3.15, pp.109--110: contraction, strict pullbacks and synchronized descent datum.

proof.text: Induct on the level $i$, with claim $A_i\simeq U\times_XB_i$ and log structure the strict etale restriction of $M_i$. At $i=0$ this is $u$. Given the claim, apply the coherent-log-ideal chart construction to $I_i$ on $B_i$: its saturated blowup commutes with strict etale restriction. Consequently the blowup of the restricted center on $A_i$ is $A_i\times_{B_i}B_{i+1}$, with the restricted log structure. This identifies the next recursive level with $U\times_XB_{i+1}$. The fiber-product identification is the unique one commuting with the projections. Etaleness and surjectivity of $A_i\to B_i$ follow at every level from their scheme base-change stability. This uses arbitrary etale log structures, not a Zariski hypothesis.

source.place: VIII 3.3.7--3.3.11, pp.107--108; induction on recursive strict etale pullback

proof.text: For a surjective strict etale map $v:(V,L)\to(Y,H)$, strictness identifies $L$ with the restriction of $H$, including section maps, so the ideal generated by $v^{-1}I$ is the restriction of $I\subset H$. If it is whole, then for every etale $W\to Y$ and $h\in H(W)$, its restriction to the cover $W\times_YV$ lies in $I$. The two restrictions of this section agree in $H$, hence in the subsheaf $I$; the sheaf equalizer for $I$ glues it to an element of $I(W)$ whose image is $h$, by the sheaf uniqueness for $H$. Thus $I=H$. The converse is immediate from the identity section. Apply this to each map of step 1. Hence a contracted tower loses no stage on a surjective strict etale pullback.

source.place: VIII 3.3.7--3.3.11, pp.107--108; whole-center detection by the sheaf condition

proof.text: A whole center contains $1$; every log pullback still contains $1$, so is whole. It is principal. More generally, every pullback of a principal center remains principal, so the identity log morphism satisfies the universal property of its saturated log blowup. Uniqueness in that property gives the canonical identity blowup. Nevertheless the prescribed contraction deletes exactly whole centers, not all identity blowups: a proper principal center is retained. This proves all the assertions about identity stages in the first paragraph.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.10, p.108; contraction removes only whole log ideals

proof.text: Apply the identity comparison of the procedure to an assigned tower of length $r$. Its source is the same assigned tower, while its contracted pullback has length $r-k$, where $k$ is the number of whole centers. The identity law for the comparison count map forces $k=0$. Thus every assigned tower is contracted. On the empty input every sheaf of sets has a singleton set of sections on its only etale object, by the sheaf condition for the empty covering. Hence every log ideal there equals the log structure. A contracted tower on that input can therefore have no stage, and has length zero.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8 and proof of 3.3.15, pp.108--110; identity comparison and empty input

proof.text: Write $p_1,p_2:R\to U$ and $q_a:P\to U$ for the projections. The $p_j$ and the projections $P\to R$ are surjective etale, since they are base changes of $u$ or of its base changes. Their log structures are the strict restrictions from $X$; successive restrictions agree on each relative etale test object, so these maps are strict. The diagonal $\delta:U\to R$ is etale since $p_1\delta=1_U$ and $p_1$ are etale, by etale cancellation. It too is strict, as the two restriction maps become the identity after $p_1\delta=1_U$. All these source and target inputs are charted admissible by the hypotheses, so all their prescribed procedure comparisons are available.

source.place: VIII proof of 3.3.15, pp.109--110; the strict etale Cech diagram

proof.text: By step 4, $S=\mathcal T(U)$ is contracted. Applying steps 1--2 to $p_j$ shows that its full pullbacks have the same $n$ stages, with no deletion. The prescribed comparisons are therefore ordered isomorphisms $c_j:p_j^*S\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal T(R)$. Set $\theta=c_2^{-1}c_1$. The comparisons preserve the actual centers by the definition of a procedure, so this composite preserves them as ideal subsheaves, not just as isomorphism classes of blowups. The retained index maps are identities on the one ordered set of $n$ stages.

source.place: VIII proof of 3.3.15, pp.109--110; full overlap comparisons after synchronization

proof.text: Let $d:\delta^*\mathcal T(R)\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ be the comparison for the diagonal. Although the diagonal need not be surjective, this comparison has no deletions: its target has length $n$ and its source tower before contraction has length $n$. The composition law, applied to $p_j\delta=1_U$, gives $d\,\delta^*c_j=1_S$ for both $j$. Hence $\delta^*\theta=(\delta^*c_2)^{-1}\delta^*c_1=1_S$, using the identity and composition identifications of the procedure.

source.place: VIII proof of 3.3.15, pp.109--110; diagonal identity from functorial comparisons

proof.text: For $a<b$ let $r_{ab}:P\to R$ select factors $a,b$, and let $e_{ab}:r_{ab}^*\mathcal T(R)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal T(P)$ be its comparison. No deletion occurs because $r_{ab}$ is surjective and the assigned tower on $R$ is contracted. The composition law identifies $e_{ab}r_{ab}^*c_1$ with the comparison $b_a:q_a^*S\to\mathcal T(P)$, and $e_{ab}r_{ab}^*c_2$ with $b_b$. Therefore $\theta_{ab}=b_b^{-1}b_a$ and $\theta_{23}\theta_{12}=b_3^{-1}b_2b_2^{-1}b_1=b_3^{-1}b_1=\theta_{13}$. These are equations of ordered log maps preserving the actual centers. Together with step 7 they give the asserted uncontracted descent datum. For $n=0$ the same formulas involve only the initial level and still apply.

source.place: VIII proof of 3.3.15, pp.109--110; triple-overlap cocycle by cancellation

proof_origin.place: VIII 3.3.7--3.3.11, pp.107--108 and descent reduction in proof of 3.3.15, pp.109--110; explicit sheaf and comparison-map arguments expanding the source

The source says contraction removes exactly the blowups along I=M_X, that log blowups are compatible with strict morphisms, and that the reduction is 'by descent'. The item writes out the descent datum hidden in that sentence, which matches the parent's mapping of old steps 1, 4 and 5. Every theorem cited is in the unit sk-i-curve-zero; the rest are definitions or Mathlib leaves, so no tool_uses are needed. No SGA. Step checks. (1) Induction A_i≅U×_X B_i: lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction gives the fs universal blowup and its commutation with strict étale restriction for arbitrary étale log structures. B_{i+1} is identified with it by the universal property. The base-change leaves give étale and surjective. It correctly avoids lem-trf-strict-log-blowup-cartesian, which needs a Zariski log structure; this answers the parent's advisory. (2) Whole-center detection by gluing in the subsheaf I over the covering W×_Y V→W: correct, and it really uses surjectivity. (3) Identity blowup of principal centers; contraction deletes only whole ones. Tested on the standard log point with N and the ideal generated by its generator: proper and principal, so retained. (4) The identity count law gives k=0. On ∅ the empty covering makes every ideal whole, so the length is 0. (5) The p_j and P→R maps are surjective étale. δ is étale by cancellation (p_1δ=1) and strict because all objects carry restrictions of M; δ is correctly not claimed surjective. (6) c_j are ordered center-preserving isomorphisms and θ=c_2^{-1}c_1. (7) The length count shows no deletions along δ, and d·δ^*c_j=1 gives δ^*θ=1. (8) I re-derived θ_ab=b_b^{-1}b_a and the cocycle θ_23θ_12=θ_13.
